Both responses correctly compute P(condition | positive) = 90/981 ≈ 9.2%, using the same 10,000-person breakdown: 90 true positives and 891 false positives. Both are under 120 words. Response A states the key insight directly: false positives from the large healthy group outnumber true positives from the small affected group. Response B leads with the answer and names the base rate fallacy, which is useful added context. Neither has a substantive advantage in correctness, reasoning, or clarity.

Verdict: TIE
